MAST30027: Metropolis-Hastings (MH) algorithm and Gibbs Sampler

Week 11

Objectives of the Tutorial/Lab By the end of this tutorial, you should be able to:

  • Derive conditional distributions for bivariate normal models.
  • Implement the Gibbs sampler.
  • Assess the effect of the proposal step size on the performance of the MH algorithm.
  • Evaluate the performance of MH using Markov chain outputs: checking autocorrelation, effective sample size, convergence, acceptance rates.

Question 2

Metropolis-Hastings [We already solved problems (a), (b), and (c) in the week 10. This week, solve the problem (d), (e), and (f).]

Recall that 𝐗=(X1X2)∼N(𝛍,𝚺)\mathbf{X} = \begin{pmatrix} X_1 \\ X_2 \end{pmatrix} \sim N(\boldsymbol\mu, \boldsymbol\Sigma), with 𝛍=(μ1μ2)\boldsymbol\mu = \begin{pmatrix} \mu_1 \\ \mu_2 \end{pmatrix} and 𝚺=(σ12σ12σ12σ22)\boldsymbol\Sigma = \begin{pmatrix} \sigma^2_1 & \sigma_{12} \\ \sigma_{12} & \sigma^2_2 \end{pmatrix}, if and only if 𝐗\mathbf{X} has joint density f𝛍,𝚺(𝐱)=12π|𝚺|1/2exp(−12(𝐱−𝛍)T𝚺−1(𝐱−𝛍)), f_{\boldsymbol\mu, \boldsymbol\Sigma}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac 1{2\pi|\boldsymbol\Sigma|^{1/2}} \exp\left( -\frac{1}{2} (\mathbf{x} - \boldsymbol\mu)^T \boldsymbol\Sigma^{-1} (\mathbf{x} - \boldsymbol\mu) \right), where 𝐱=(x1x2)\mathbf{x} = \begin{pmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{pmatrix}.

Write an R function that evaluates the density of a bivariate normal distribution. The function should take as input the point 𝐱\mathbf{x}, the mean 𝛍\boldsymbol\mu and the covariance matrix 𝚺\boldsymbol\Sigma.

You will find the functions solve and det useful.

💡 Solution 
dbinorm <- function(x, mu, Si) {
  # x and mu are vectors length 2 and Si a 2x2 matric
  # returns the density at x of a bivariate normal mean mu var Si
  exp(-t(x - mu)%*%solve(Si, x - mu)/2)/2/pi/sqrt(det(Si))
}
You can check that it is working by noting that dbinorm(c(1,1), c(0,0), matrix(c(1,0,0,1),2,2)) gives the same answer as dnorm(1)^2.

💡 Solution 
set.seed(100)
# Metropolis-Hastings simulation of a bivariate normal
# inputs
mu <- c(0, 0)                     # mean
Si <- matrix(c(4, 1, 1, 4), 2, 2) # variance
iterations <- 1000      # sample size
startvalue <- c(6, -6)  # initial value
sd <- 2.5               # std-dev for proposal chain
# main loop
chain <- matrix(nrow = iterations+1, ncol = 2)
chain[1,] <- startvalue
accepted <- 0 # counts num accepted proposals
for (i in 1:iterations){
  proposal <- rnorm(2, chain[i,], sd)
  prob <- dbinorm(proposal, mu, Si)/dbinorm(chain[i,], mu, Si)
  if (is.nan(prob)) prob <- 0
  if (runif(1) < prob) {
    chain[i+1,] <- proposal
    accepted <- accepted + 1
    } else {
      chain[i+1,] <- chain[i,]
    }
}

# acceptance rate
accepted/iterations
[1] 0.457
# 2D density plot
library(MASS)
chain_density <- kde2d(chain[,1], chain[,2], n = 15)
persp(chain_density, phi = 30, theta = 30, d = 5, xlab = "x", ylab = "y", zlab = "f(x,y)", ticktype = "detailed")

The acceptance rate was 46% (this will vary a little every time you run the program).

To check that the output looks ok, I have plotted (a kernel density estimate of) the joint density. Easier than plotting a joint density would be to plot histograms/densities of the marginal samples, using hist or density.

💡 Solution 
# cumulative averages
par(mfrow=c(2,1), mar=c(4,4,1,1))
plot(chain[,1], xlab = "iteration", ylab = "x1")
cumavg1 <- cumsum(chain[,1])/1:(iterations + 1)
lines(1:(iterations + 1), cumavg1, col = "red", lwd=2)
plot(chain[,2], xlab = "iteration", ylab = "x2")
cumavg2 <- cumsum(chain[,2])/1:(iterations + 1)
lines(1:(iterations + 1), cumavg2, col = "red", lwd=2)

📈 Plotting it using ggplot2 
library(ggplot2)
trace_df <- data.frame(
  iteration=rep(seq_len(iterations+1), 2),
  value=c(chain[,1], chain[,2]),
  cumulative_average=c(cumavg1, cumavg2),
  variable=rep(c("x1", "x2"), each=iterations+1))
ggplot(trace_df, aes(iteration)) +
  geom_point(aes(y=value)) + 
  geom_line(aes(y=cumulative_average), colour="red", linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~variable, ncol=1, scales="free_y") +
  labs(y=NULL) + 
  theme_minimal()

We can write a general function for the MH algorithm which allows for adjusting the parameter values in the target distribution as well as the proposal distribution. Run the algorithm using different standard deviation of the proposal and compare their trace plots, acceptance rates, and autocorrelations.

💡 Incomplete solution for R code 
# reuse the density function we defined in previous session
dbinorm <- function(x, mu, Si) {
  # x and mu are vectors length 2 and Si a 2x2 matric
  # returns the density at x of a bivariate normal mean mu var Si
  exp(-t(x - mu)%*%solve(Si, x - mu)/2)/2/pi/sqrt(det(Si))
}

# we can define a function for the MH algorithm which allows us to adjust the proposal sd
rbinormMH <- function(mu, Si, iterations = 1000, startvalue = c(6, -6), sd = 2.5) {
  # mu = mean, Si = variance, startvalue = initial value, sd = std-dev
  # for proposal chain
  chain <- matrix(nrow = iterations+1, ncol = 2)
  chain[1,] <- startvalue
  accepted <- 0
  for (i in 1:iterations){
    # write the steps we need within the chain, need to update `chain` and `accepted`
    
    
    
    
    
  }
  attributes(chain) <- list(dim = c(iterations+1,2),
                            p_accept = accepted/iterations,
                            rho1 = cor(chain[-(iterations+1),1], chain[-1,1]),
                            rho2 = cor(chain[-(iterations+1),2], chain[-1,2]))
  return(chain)
}
